summary.text: Nellie Pou is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 9th Congressional District, elected in 2024 to succeed the late Rep. Bill Pascrell and sworn in on January 3, 2025.

She spent decades in Paterson city government and then served 14 years in the New Jersey General Assembly and 13 years in the New Jersey Senate before running for Congress. She serves on the House Committees on Homeland Security and on Transportation and Infrastructure and is seeking a second term.

paragraphs.text: Pou was born in Paterson, New Jersey, on May 20, 1956, and studied at Kean College, Rutgers University, and the University of Virginia.

She worked for the City of Paterson for more than 40 years, according to her official biography, including as Director of Human Resources and as Business Administrator; Ballotpedia lists her as chair of the city's Department of Human Resources from 1983 to 1997.

She also served on the New Jersey Task Force on Child Abuse and Neglect and the Passaic County Planning and Policy Partnership Committee, and on state commissions including the New Jersey Complete Count Commission for the 2020 Census and the New Jersey Criminal Sentencing and Disposition Commission.

Pou entered the New Jersey General Assembly in 1997 as the first woman and first Latina to represent the 35th District. She chaired the Assembly Appropriations Committee, served as Deputy Speaker, and spent 14 years in the Assembly.

She was first elected to the New Jersey Senate in 2011 and re-elected in 2013, 2017, 2021, and 2023, serving 13 years, including as Senate Majority Caucus Chair and Chair of the Senate Commerce Committee.
She chaired the New Jersey Legislative Latino Caucus and was the first New Jersey legislator to serve as President of the National Hispanic Caucus of State Legislators.
Pou was selected in August 2024 to replace Rep. Bill Pascrell on the Democratic ballot after his death, and she won the November 2024 general election 50.8% to 45.9%.

She was sworn into the U.S. House on January 3, 2025, as the first Latina from New Jersey in Congress, and serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee (as Vice Ranking Member of its Aviation Subcommittee) and the Homeland Security Committee.
She received an honorary doctorate from William Paterson University in May 2024 and was named to InsiderNJ's list of New Jersey's 100 Policymakers in 2020.
